scope: Canonical Git source held through internal catalog/source handoff, including acquiring-process-only clone cleanup after inherited context unwind.

resolved.assessment: Actual _clone_git_source captures clone_owner_pid before temporary acquisition and gates exception cleanup by that PID. Actual _open_source captures source_owner_pid before acquisition and gates final clone-parent deletion there. Child unwinding no longer deletes the acquiring parent's canonical checkout; same-process normal/error cleanup remains on the original path and exceptions continue to propagate.
resolved.evidence: Independent maintained real fork case executes inherited complete context unwind, verifies child result0, parent successfully completes actual copy and canonical Git provenance afterward, and parent normal exit removes the clone. Both surrounding modules also pass.
resolved.qualification: Original dependency cleanup behavior was inherited into the new long-lived guarantee; repair is at the actual destructive owner. This closes the specific fork-unwind finding, not general filesystem deletion/GC or every acquisition interrupt scenario.

source_assessment: Four source-lease integration production subjects are unchanged from initial exact review; shared ledger, canonical ref, original input/census witnesses and pure source lifetime closure assessment remains applicable.
PID checks guard only destructive clone cleanup. They do not authorize child reads/effects or skip normal parent cleanup.
Inherited source/copy registries revoke in child-local memory, source pins close only child descriptor copies, and actual staged reservation retention closes descriptor copies without name deletion.

Existing journal writer mutex cleanup separately checks acquiring PID before explicit unlock, avoiding release of the parent's shared open-file-description lock; this helper was source-inspected, not a new mutex-contender test.

Ordinary local-source _open_source branch is unchanged. Parent Git acquisition error path still runs the same cleanup under an always-matching acquiring PID; canonical process deadline/output and Git ref behavior remain unchanged.
